answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a stake in shared escrow before trading. New identities start on a narrow ledge: they may only take small jobs, and each completed job moves a little collateral into a reputation haven that only that agent can spend. Spawning a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand separate stakes, so the attacker pays real capital per identity. A public jetty of signed attestations lets peers verify history before hiring, so fresh sybils cannot borrow trust they never earned.
